attributes.translation: I don't want to go play in the park.
attributes.nuance_translation: A word that primarily points out things that the speaker wants to do.

attributes.body:
たい is an auxiliary verb that is used to express things that you would like to do (want). To use たい, it needs to be added to the same conjugation base form of a verb that ます would be attached to.

When using たい, the thing that is 'wanted' can either be marked with を, or が. The difference in nuance is that something marked with が is considered to be wanted more. たい is conjugated in the same way as い-Adjectives, meaning that the negative, past, or past-negative forms may also be used.

たい is only used for expressing things that 'you' want, or repeating information/asking questions about what other people want. It may not be used to make guesses about what other people 'may' want, unless asking them directly.

Caution

たい is not used to tell other people that you want them to do something. This is done with ～てほしい.

Caution

たい is not usually used when giving invitations (asking someone if they want to do something with you). In these cases ～ませんか is far more natural.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Verbs you want to do with 「たい」

attributes.body: The たい form expresses personal desires, such as 日本に行きたい ('I want to go to Japan'), though, the たい form is typically not used for expressing others' desires. One way that we can comment on another person's desires, however, is to use the そう form, meaning 'appears to.' For example 日本に行きたそう can be used to mean 'They seem to want to go to Japan.'

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: ませんか is a polite way to extend an invitation, similar to 'Wouldn't you like to...?' in English. For example, 何か食べませんか？ ('Won't you eat something?') might be used when politely offering food to a guest. Note that unlike English, the たい form ('Do you want to…?') isn't typically used to invite someone in Japanese—何か食べたいですか？ simply asks if the person wants to eat something.

first_relatable.title: ませんか
first_relatable.meaning: Won't you, Would you not, Why don't we

attributes.body: Both the たい form and がほしい express desires, similar to the English 'want.' The difference is that たい is used with verbs to express one's desire to perform some action, while がほしい is used after nouns to express one's desire for an object. For example, 日本に行きたい means 'I want to go to Japan' (desire to do something), while お金がほしい means 'I want money' (desire for an object).

second_relatable.title: がほしい
second_relatable.meaning: To want something, To be in need of

attributes.body: The たい form expresses personal desires, like バナナが食べたい ('I want to eat a banana'). がる, on the other hand, is used to show that someone else seems to want something, like 食べたがっている ('[He/she] seems like they want to eat'). The たい form is generally not used for others' desires unless the subject has explicitly made their desire clear.

second_relatable.title: がる
second_relatable.meaning: To feel, To think, To act as if, To want, To desire

attributes.body: The たい form expresses personal desires, such as 日本に行きたい ('I want to go to Japan'). がる, on the other hand, is a suffix that shows when someone else appears to want something, like 日本に行きたがっている ('They seem like they want to go to Japan'). The たい form is typically not used for expressing others' desires unless quoting the subject.

Both たい and てほしい express a desire, with one key difference. The たい form is used to express your own desires, similar to the English 'I want to...' while てほしい expresses your desires for other people, or in other words, 'I want you to…' For example, 見たい would express your desire to see something, while 見てほしい would be used if you want someone else to take a look.
